proof_audit.finding: Normalization gives E r=1; integrable log ratios and nonnegative r−1−log r prove the gap and equality. Equal densities imply equal labels only with injectivity. Conditional equality is only almost everywhere on the actual covariate support; no causal claim follows.

Common positive support, twice differentiable densities and first/second derivative domination license both derivatives of normalization. Score outer-product and Hessian integrability are explicit. Misspecification uses the actual law and separates A from B; unconditional zero score does not imply conditional zero score.

Continuity and compactness give an attained maximizer, with measurable selection imposed explicitly. Uniform convergence and a strict compact separation prove consistency before the Hessian segment is used. Interiority, uniform local Hessians and nonsingular curvature yield a bounded inverse and the rate from the centered score CLT. The positive A-inverse score sign is correct.

The square-integrable Lipschitz score envelope bounds the average squared plug-in error; Cauchy–Schwarz handles both outer-product cross terms. Hessian replacement is separate. Positive limiting contrast variance is required for studentization. Approximate objective and approximate score conditions are correctly assigned different roles.

Bounded regressors and compact convex coefficients supply bounded derivatives and probabilities away from endpoints. Conditional KL, monotone link and E xx-prime rank identify the coefficient. Positive expected weighted rank supplies curvature. The separated sample has a monotone unattained unrestricted likelihood and a constrained boundary fit. Probit formulas do not assert an unproved general probit theorem.

The expansion includes empirical-X fluctuation and the parameter influence jointly, with local derivative convergence and finite second moments. The covariance cancellation uses conditional centering. The offset counterexample has nonzero Cov(h,s), so its negative cross term matters. Known target weights describe a distinct estimator. A discrete X law identifies support-point conditional means, not a unique interpolating derivative.

The exponential convexity gap proves mean-criterion identification without a Poisson law. Compact bounded-index conditions and E Y-squared finite supply the global/local envelopes, centered finite-variance score and curvature. Meat uses Y−exp(x-prime beta); omitting D changes the target despite a centered unconditional score. Population and finite-sample matrices are correctly separated.

The independent-normal construction and orthogonal rotation yield the selected joint density; integration preserves selected probability plus unselected mass. Selected-only sampling divides by Phi(a). Two tail integrals give Mills mean and selected variance, including its rho-squared term. The text proves these distributional formulas and explicitly withholds universal identification or regular selection-MLE inference.

The declared closed-support density has its maximum at a positive sample maximum. The exact maximum CDF gives the expectation, n-rate exponential gap and exact confidence coverage. The omitted moving-boundary derivative explains the formal uncentered score; mere interiority of the population parameter is insufficient.

Every required exercise method is taught or explicitly inherited from c01–c03. The open audit gives seven distinct diagnoses, repairs and evidence requirements for its at-least-six request. Teach-back and delayed checks are answered. Six-observation and eight-row asymptotic calculations are not described as exact normal calibrations.

independent_numerical_method.group_models: Binary coefficient covariance is obtained by transforming independent group log-odds, not by copying an inverse-Hessian formula. Count covariance comes from saturated conditional-mean influence vectors; row-wise A/B are checked separately.
independent_numerical_method.predictive_effects: For each of six correct-model and four misspecified-law atoms, perturb the full probability law in both directions, refit the finite logit and differentiate the resulting target numerically. The six correct-model atoms are additionally refit with the original X target distribution fixed. These are 32 finite refits and 10 distinct atom directions.
independent_numerical_method.selection: Composite 32-node Gauss–Legendre integration over the selecting latent normal uses its conditional outcome mean/variance and the independent second normal. A separate convolution recovers the density. It does not reuse the author Simpson outcome-density oracle.
independent_numerical_method.selection_bounds: Four changed-parameter cases; selecting index magnitude below one, finite means/scales and nonsingular correlations. Upper integration endpoint 10. Normal tail truncation is negligible at the stated 2e-8 moment tolerance; quadrature is numerical evidence, not a general error theorem.
independent_numerical_method.maximum: The finite tail is reconstructed as the product of individual threshold probabilities; density integration separately checks expectations at three changed sample-size/scale pairs. Exact rational pivot arithmetic checks scale invariance.
independent_numerical_method.printed_values: Every data-calc value independently reconstructed: 34 exact rational and 9 rounded anchors. Unmarked matrices and all table contracts were also checked by full reading and original-law algebra.
independent_numerical_method.strictness: Independent metadata parsing rejects duplicate members, nonfinite literals and overflowing decimal exponents. Seventeen meaningful invalid domains actually raise explicit exceptions under normal and optimized Python.
independent_numerical_method.limitations: Finite perturbation derivatives and quadrature do not prove asymptotic or identification theorems. Analytic proof reading is separate; no simulations, saved author outputs or author helper functions are oracles.
